about_role:
The South African Police Service is hiring a Police Trainee (national post). This is a contract post, paying R5,000 a month.

How to apply: NB: To apply online, please visit the South African Police Service website on: https://www.saps.gov.za and click on the link or scan the QR code provided. The step-by-step guide to apply for utilizing the SAPS electronic recruitment system are as follows: ✓ Register your account on the SAPS site; ✓ Enter your profile details through the Profile User page; ✓ Log into your account; ✓ On the home page, browse to the SAPS vacancy page link; ✓ Locate and select the job you want to apply for (i.e. TRA26/27); ✓ Enter personal details through the multi steps application process and submit your application.
Reference number to quote: TRA26/27
Closing date: 13 November 2026
Apply online on the SAPS e-Recruitment portal (erecruitment.saps.gov.za).
responsibilities:
Successful candidates will serve as functional police officials. As such, they will be deployed to carry out the following functions:
Prevent, combat and investigate crime
Maintain public order
Protect and secure the inhabitants of the Republic and their property
Uphold and enforce the law.
requirements:
A person who applies to be employed as an entry level police trainee must - Apply on the form determined by the National Commissioner and affirm under oath or by way of a solemn declaration that the particulars furnished in the application, are the truth and correct
Be a citizen of the Republic of South Africa of which documentary proof must be furnished
Be at least eighteen (18) years of age and not older than thirty-five (35) years of age at the time of the closing date for applications stipulated in the relevant advertisement, of which documentary proof must be furnished
Submit himself or herself to a physical and medical examination as determined by the National Commissioner and must be found to be physically, medically and mentally fit for appointment in the service
Undergo a psychological and integrity assessment as determined by the National Commissioner and be found to comply with the profile of a police official
Be in possession of a grade 12 school certificate or equivalent qualification of which documentary proof must be furnished
Be proficient in at least English and one other official language
Be prepared to take the oath of office
Be prepared to undergo such training as, where and when determined by the National Commissioner
Not have any tattoo marks which will be visible when wearing any uniform of the Service
Not have been declared unfit to possess a firearm
Not have any previous criminal convictions or any pending criminal cases
Not have been dismissed for serious misconduct from the employ of a previous employer, where such dismissal relates to any act of dishonesty or violence; sexual harassment or is drug related
Allow a buccal sample and his or her fingerprints to be taken and verified against the criminal record system
Allow background enquiries to be made
Be prepared to undergo security vetting and obtain the level of security clearance determined by the National Commissioner; and Be prepared to serve anywhere in the Republic.
Applicants in possession of a relevant three (3) years tertiary qualification (NQF 6 or higher) i.e. Criminal Law / Policing / Forensic investigation etc.
Applicants in possession of other three (3) years tertiary qualification (NQF 6 or higher
Applicants in possession of Grade 12 school certificate with the minimum requirements for admission to bachelor’s degree
All applicants will be subjected to a fitness, psychometric and integrity testing as well as medical evaluation and will be interviewed during the recruitment, selection and enlistment process. The SAPS will also verify the qualifications, drivers’ licence, where applicable, citizenship and residential address of each applicant.
Applicants will be subjected to a vetting process which will include security screening, reference checking, social media presence and fingerprint verification to establish whether any illicit activity has been recorded or is pending against candidates.
Applicants who previously served in a Government Department and who were dismissed because of misconduct will not be considered for appointment in the South African Police Service (SAPS).
In view of the physical demands of the Basic Police Development Learning Programme, applicants with chronic diseases, physical impairments or any other health condition that may lead to interruption of the training programme, may be excluded from participation in the programme. Should applicants fail to disclose any health condition it may result in their withdrawal from the programme on the determination thereof.

about_role:
AECI is hiring a Vice President: Internal Controls - Financial Reporting, based in Sandton.
To provide strategic leadership, governance, and oversight of the Group's Internal Financial Controls (IFC) framework, ensuring compliance with JSE Listing Requirements (Section 3.84(k)), the COSO 2013 framework, and applicable governance standards. The role is responsible for strengthening the control environment across the Group, safeguarding the integrity of financial reporting, managing financial reporting risks, driving continuous improvement in control effectiveness, and providing assurance to executive leadership and the Audit & Risk Committee on the adequacy and effectiveness of internal financial controls.
responsibilities:
JSE 3.84(k) Compliance Leadership and Oversight:
Lead the planning, execution, and management of the company’s Internal Financial Controls (IFC) compliance program to meet JSE Listings Requirements (specifically Section 3.84(k)), ensuring timely and effective completion of reporting cycles.
Support the Group Chief Financial Officer in driving continuous improvement in the IFC program maturity, scalability, and risk coverage in alignment with the King V Report on Corporate Governance.
Risk and Control Assessment:
Oversee the scoping, risk assessment, and control identification process for all Business Units and Group functions in collaboration with key stakeholders, including Group Risk and Group Internal Audit, for final approval by the Group Chief Financial Officer.
Evaluate new risks, with the support of Group Risk, arising from organisational changes, acquisitions, systems implementations, or regulatory updates (e.g., Companies Act of South Africa, governance changes, tax regulations in various jurisdictions etc.).
Internal Control Design and Testing:
Ensure proper design and implementation of internal controls over financial reporting (ICFR/IFC), focusing on key controls that will ensure high assurance coverage levels for all financial balances included in the primary financial statements (i.e., Statement of Financial Position; Statement of Comprehensive Income, Statement of Changes in Equity, and Statement of Cash Flow).

about_role:
Heineken Beverages is hiring an Automation Engineer, based in Johannesburg.
The key purpose of this role is to provide structured, strategic and leadership within the automation and control discipline across Heineken Beverages manufacturing operations. The role develops and governs automation standards, architecture, frameworks and lifecycle practices; influences site and project decisions; improves manufacturing reliability and performance; strengthens PCD cybersecurity; and enables the controlled implementation and enhancement of digital manufacturing technologies. The role works across sites and functions to ensure automation solutions are safe, reliable, maintainable, secure, integrated, scalable and aligned with Heineken requirements and long-term business priorities.
responsibilities:
Automation Manufacturing Reliability and Continuous Improvement:
Provide cross-site technical leadership to improve the reliability, maintainability and performance of automation and control systems.
Establish and govern reliability standards, maintenance strategies and performance measures for PLC, SCADA, HMI, industrial networks, drives, instrumentation and associated control infrastructure.
Analyse systemic failures, repeat breakdowns and automation-related production losses; lead structured root cause analysis and ensure sustainable corrective and preventive actions are implemented.
Support sites with complex or high-impact automation incidents while strengthening site capability and ownership.
Identify and prioritise opportunities to improve throughput, quality, energy performance, process stability, OPI and cost through automation and advanced control.
Develop reusable troubleshooting practices, standard diagnostics, technical guidance and lessons-learned mechanisms across the manufacturing network.
Automation Projects and Obsolescence Management:
Provide technical assurance and lifecycle governance for automation capital projects, upgrades and obsolescence programmes.
Define automation project requirements, design principles, acceptance criteria and handover standards.
Review and approve control philosophies, functional design specifications, architectures, software designs, network designs and supplier proposals for compliance with approved standards.
Participate in design reviews, risk assessments, FAT, SAT, commissioning, performance verification and operational handover for strategic projects.
Develop and maintain automation asset lifecycle and obsolescence frameworks, site risk profiles, technology roadmaps and prioritised replacement plans.
Automation Technology, Architecture and Integration:
Define and govern fit-for-purpose automation technologies and integration patterns across the control and manufacturing landscape.
Own and maintain reference architectures, approved technology standards, software libraries, naming conventions, interface principles and engineering practices for automation and control systems.
Evaluate emerging and existing technologies against business value, cybersecurity, interoperability, supportability, scalability and lifecycle requirements.
Ensure reliable integration between field devices, control systems, SCADA, historians, MES, utilities platforms, reporting solutions and approved enterprise services.
Guide industrial communication and data integration using approved protocols, segmented architectures and clearly defined ownership boundaries between OT and IT.
Maintain strategic relationships with OEMs, system integrators and technology partners; influence roadmaps and ensure solutions remain aligned with Heineken architecture and support models.
Create governance mechanisms for deviations, technical decisions, solution assurance and controlled introduction of new technology.
PCD Cybersecurity and Compliance:
Strengthen cybersecurity and compliance within the Process Control Domain through standards, risk management and technical governance.
Translate Heineken PCD security requirements into practical automation engineering standards, implementation roadmaps and assurance controls.
Govern secure network segmentation, access control, remote access, backup and restore, patching, malware protection, account management, logging and recovery practices for automation assets.
Support PCD risk assessments, audits, vulnerability remediation and incident response, ensuring actions are prioritised according to operational and business risk.
Embed security-by-design into automation projects, system changes, supplier access and technology lifecycle decisions.
Define evidence, documentation and compliance routines required to demonstrate that controls are implemented, sustained and periodically tested.
Collaborate with PCD Security, IT, site engineering and external partners to resolve risks without compromising safety, quality or production continuity.
Digital Manufacturing Implementation and Enhancement:
Enable sustainable digital manufacturing solutions by ensuring robust automation data foundations, controlled integration and measurable operational value.
Provide automation leadership for historian, MES, OPI, energy, condition monitoring, analytics and other approved digital manufacturing initiatives.
Define data acquisition, contextualisation, tag, interface, time synchronisation, data quality and ownership standards from shop-floor systems to authorised digital platforms.
Ensure digital solutions are industrialised, supportable, cybersecure and integrated into site operating and maintenance routines rather than remaining isolated pilots.
Partner with operations, engineering, digital, data and IT teams to translate business problems into scalable automation and data solutions.
Assess solution performance after implementation and drive enhancements based on adoption, reliability, data quality and realised business benefits.
Standards, Governance, Capability and Strategic Influence:
Build a consistent and sustainable automation engineering capability across Heineken Beverages through governance, assurance and knowledge leadership.
Develop, maintain and deploy automation policies, standards, frameworks, specifications, templates and technical procedures aligned with global and local requirements.
Establish governance forums, compliance assessments, maturity reviews and performance reporting to provide visibility of automation risks, priorities and progress.
Influence investment plans and management decisions by presenting clear technical risk, lifecycle, cost and business-impact information.
Provide coaching, technical mentoring and structured capability development for site automation engineers, technicians, project engineers and relevant stakeholders.
Facilitate cross-site communities of practice, knowledge sharing, benchmarking and replication of proven solutions.
Define competency expectations and support succession and training for the automation and control discipline.
Act as a recognised subject matter expert and escalation point, balancing enterprise standardisation with site requirements and operational realities.
Safety, Health, Environment and Quality:
Ensure that automation strategies, designs, changes and work practices protect people, product, plant, information and the environment.
Apply management-of-change, functional safety, quality, environmental and legal requirements to automation engineering activities.
Ensure control system modifications are appropriately assessed, tested, approved, documented, backed up and recoverable before release to production.
Promote safe engineering behaviours and ensure suppliers and partners comply with site and Heineken SHE requirements.
requirements:
Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronic Engineering, Mechatronics, Process Control, Instrumentation, Automation or a related engineering discipline.
Relevant professional registration, postgraduate qualification or recognized automation, industrial networking, cybersecurity or project certification would be an added advantage.
Minimum 10 years relevant experience in industrial automation and control within a manufacturing or process environment, including experience with PLC, SCADA/HMI, industrial networks, drives, instrumentation and system integration.
Demonstrated experience in automation projects, reliability improvement, technology lifecycle or obsolescence management and cross-functional technical leadership.
Experience operating across multiple manufacturing sites, developing standards or providing technical governance at business, regional or Centre of Excellence level would be an added advantage.

The Parole Board is an independent body whose main aim is to protect the public by risk assessing offenders to decide whether they can be safely released into the community. The main role of a Chair (and Vice in the chairs absence) is decision making. Decision making in light of a number of factors, that is:- rights of the offender (as far as the right to be considered in light of relevant legislation), calculation of the minimum detention period, understanding of criminal justice value chain, court papers, sentencing remarks, copy of the judgment, copy of the warrant of detention, case law, SAP 69 and 62, understanding the various reports by the DCS professionals, understanding of the rehabilitation process, risk assessment, victim/community empathy, public safety etc. Applicants who have retired from the Public Service with a specific determination that they cannot be reappointed or have been declared medically unfit will not be considered. Term of office will be for a period of five (5) years or as may be determined by the Minister in line with Section 74 (7) of the Correctional Services Act, Act 111 of 1998. Applications: Applications must be submitted on the Z83 form (Public Service application form) accessible on the link below and must be completed in full. Only a detailed CV should be attached to your application form. Only shortlisted candidates will be required to submit certified copies not older than 6 months of qualifications and other related documents on or before the day of the interview. Applicants must note that further checks will be conducted once they are shortlisted and that their appointment is subject to positive outcomes on these checks, which include security clearance, security vetting, qualification verification and criminal records verification. Candidates must comply with the minimum appointment requirements. CV’s should be aligned to reflect one’s degree of compliance with the advertisement requirements and responsibilities. The Department of Correctional Services reserves the right not to fill these posts. Persons with disabilities are encouraged to apply. Candidates must comply with the minimum appointment requirements. CV’s should be aligned to reflect one’s degree of compliance with the advertisement requirements and responsibilities. The Department of Correctional Services reserves the right not to fill these posts.
responsibilities:
Analyse and critically evaluate information in order to identify continuing risk/dangerous-ness in an individual offender’s case, where information may come from a variety of sources including electronic and paper documents, electronic updates and evidence given at oral hearings.
Apply knowledge and judgement to offenders’ cases in order to decide whether they can safely be released into the community and to set conditions where release is appropriate.
Oversee the hearing of cases in order to assess risk.
Work collaboratively with other parole members in order to make judgements about the available evidence and to provide a concise and structured summary of relevant factors in reaching a decision or recommendation.
Facilitate report writing, draft reasoned summaries and decisions.
Be an effective ambassador for the Parole Board when representing it at hearings or any other event.
Facilitate administrative roles associated with preparation for hearings, hearings and revocations/cancellations, public education on parole, facilitate invitation of victims to hearings including court attendance as a result of litigation by offenders.
requirements:
A recognized and appropriate NQF level 7 qualification in any Criminal Justice field, Social Sciences or related.
Previous 5 years’ experience in management or decision-making position.
Demonstrable experience of and ability to conduct effective evidence-based decision making, weighing facts and evidence, analysing and critically evaluating large volumes of complex information and identifying key issues, within tight deadlines and working on your own initiative.
Demonstrable independence of mind and sound judgement, with the ability to make evidence-based decisions that are accurately documented.
Excellent interpersonal skills: The ability to gain respect and maintain rapport through effective communication and influencing skills - with the confidence to challenge opinions where necessary, work collegiately and resolve differences to reach sound decisions.
Excellent communication skills, both written and oral: The ability to communicate sensitively and effectively with a wide range of individuals, varying your approach as necessary and treating others with respect, to listen actively and evaluate replies in order to probe issues.
Excellent written skills: The ability to draft well-formed written reports which summarizes evidence in support of a decision or recommendation.
Demonstrable high standards of corporate and personal integrity and conduct, such as a strong commitment to fairness, equality and the ethos of supporting the wider public or community good through your contributions.
High levels of time management, organizational and administrative skills, together with strong personal motivation and commitment to professional self-development.
Evidence of experience of any aspect of the criminal justice system and an understanding of the importance of the victim’s perspective.
Previous experience in management or decision-making position.

responsibilities:

job_title: Senior Credit Manager, Natural Resources, Origination, CIB
about_role:
Standard Bank is hiring a Senior Credit Manager, Natural Resources, Origination, CIB, based in Johannesburg, Gauteng.
To provide independent credit risk leadership and transaction support for Natural Resources financing opportunities across South Africa and the broader African continent. The role works closely with Coverage, Product and Transaction teams during the origination, structuring and execution of transactions to ensure that key risks are identified early, properly assessed and appropriately mitigated.
The incumbent will play an important role in shaping transactions before formal credit submission by providing clear risk insight, challenging proposed structures and assumptions, and influencing outcomes that are aligned with the Bank’s risk appetite and strategic objectives. The role requires close engagement with internal and external stakeholders, including clients, sponsors, advisers and transaction teams, to support sustainable financing solutions while preserving credit quality and portfolio integrity.
As a subject matter expert within Natural Resources, the incumbent will provide informed credit input on sector trends, emerging risks, commodity markets, operating environments and industry developments across the relevant geographies. The role is expected to support high-quality credit decision-making through robust analysis, sound judgement and well-reasoned recommendations that ensure transactions are appropriately structured and capable of delivering acceptable risk-adjusted returns. This includes the review of term sheets, legal agreements, security and transaction documents to ensure risks are appropriately identified, mitigated and documented.
This role works closely with Environmental, Governance and Social Risk advisory to identify and assess ESG risks associated with transactions and ensure alignment with Bank policy, sector appetite and sustainability objectives.
The incumbent will lead the presentation and discussion of transactions at Credit Committees and other senior approval forums, providing clear recommendations supported by robust analysis and balanced risk assessment.
In this role the incumbent will originate credit applications for new transactions and when necessary, prepare or evaluate annual review credit applications, ensuring transactions remain aligned with the Bank's risk appetite, policy requirements and strategic objectives. The incumbent to provide coaching, technical guidance and leadership to less experienced credit professionals, contributing to capability development across the Natural Resources credit team.
Success in the role will be measured by the quality of credit risk assessment, the strength of risk challenge, the ability to influence transaction outcomes, and the contribution made to growing a sustainable, well-managed and resilient Natural Resources credit portfolio.
requirements:
Professional Qualifications:
Preference will be given to candidates holding a CA(SA), CFA, FRM, or other relevant professional qualification demonstrating advanced expertise in financial analysis, risk assessment, and transaction evaluation.
Type of Qualification: Post Graduate Degree
Field of Study: Business Commerce, Finance, Accounting, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, or a related discipline.
Experience Required:
8 to 10 years’ experience in credit risk, preferably with meaningful exposure to the Natural Resources sector, including mining and metals, oil and gas, or related sectors. A strong track record of working on new, complex and structured transactions across South Africa and the broader African continent is required. Experience in project finance, corporate lending, global market derivative products, leveraged finance, trade finance, or diversified industrials would be advantageous.
Well-developed knowledge of financial markets, commodity markets, macroeconomic trends, and the regional geographies in which the portfolio operates. The incumbent should be able to assess sector developments, country-specific risks, technical feasibility and transaction-level risks in a manner that supports sound credit decision-making.
Thorough conceptual and practical knowledge of credit procedures, credit policies, delegated authority frameworks, credit rating methodologies, Basel requirements, regulatory expectations, and compliance standards. Strong understanding of banking products and facilities that give rise to counterparty credit risk is required.

All sections of the Z83 must be completed (in full, accurately, legibly, honestly, signed and dated), and accompanied by a comprehensive / detailed Curriculum Vitae. Only shortlisted candidates will be required to submit certified copies of qualifications and other related documents on or before the day of the interview which should not be older than six months. The Curriculum Vitae and Z83 form must have at least three (3) contactable references. Failure to comply with the above instructions will result in applications being disqualified. Applicants applying for more than one post must submit a separate form Z83 (as well as the documentation mentioned above) in respect of each post being applied for. If an applicant wishes to withdraw an application, it must be done in writing. Should an application be received where an applicant applies for more than one post on the same applications form, the application will only be considered for the first post indicated on the application and not for any of the other posts. Applicants who participated in any other Government Internship Programmes before will not be considered. Students requiring experiential training as part of their qualification must attach a formal letter from their Tertiary Institution. Failure to submit all the requested documents will result in the application not being considered. Applicants must note that personnel suitability checks (PSC) will be conducted on the short-listed applicants, therefore will be required to give consent in terms of the POPI Act in order for the Department to conduct this exercise. Successful candidates will also be subjected to security clearance processes. Applicants who do not receive confirmation or feedback within three (3) months after the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful. Due to the large volume of responses anticipated, receipt of applications will not be acknowledged, and correspondence will be limited to shortlisted candidates only. How to apply: E-mailed to MashiloaneK@saps.gov.za Applications may be hand-delivered, as follows: 152 Johannes Ramakhoase Street, Telkom Towers North, Pretoria. Application must be deposited into the box available at the reception area. Applications forwarded by post to be addressed to The Section Head: Corporate Support, (Attention: Captain Pretorius / W/O Tshabalala), Corporate Support, South African Police Service, Private Bag X94, Pretoria, 0001.
Reference number to quote: CCL 03/2026
Closing date: 20 November 2026 at 16:00
Use the new Z83 form and attach a detailed CV.
Note: Applications must be submitted on a Z83 Form (2021 version), obtainable from http://www.dpsa.gov.za/dpsa2g/vacancies.asp, which must be accompanied with a comprehensive Curriculum Vitae. The post particulars and reference number of the post you are applying for, must be correctly specified on the application form. Please complete a separate application form for each post you wish to apply for. It is the responsibility of the applicants to submit applications timeously to the correct physical address as provided in the advertisement. Please note that applications submitted to an incorrect physical address will not be considered. Late applications will not be accepted or considered. Short-listed candidates will be required to produce originals of their Identity Document (ID), Senior Certificate and all educational qualifications obtained, service certificates from previous employers stating the occupation and motor vehicle driver’s license, before the interview. Qualifications and driver’s licences submitted will be subjected to verification with the relevant institutions. Applicants must have no previous criminal convictions or pending criminal/ departmental cases and shall allow their fingerprints to be taken and background enquiries to be made. Short-listed candidates may be subjected to a full security clearance process before or during any stage of employment. Short-listed candidates will be subjected to a vetting process which will include security screening, fingerprint screening, reference checking and verification of address, where necessary. All shortlisted candidates, including SMS, shall undertake two pre-entry assessments. One will be a practical exercise to determine a candidate’s suitability based on the post’s technical and generic requirements and the other must be an integrity (ethical conduct) assessment. Selection panels shall score both technical exercises as an additional criterion in the interview process. Short-listed candidates for appointments to certain identified posts will be vetted in terms of the Criminal Law (Sexual Offences and Related Matters) Amendment Act, 2007 (Act No 32 of 2007) and the Children’s Act, 2005 (Act No 38 of 2005). A candidate whose particulars appear in either the National Register for Sex Offenders or Part B of the Child Protection Register, will be disqualified from appointment. Candidates are expected to disclose if he/ she is a respondent in an interim or final protection order in terms of the Domestic Violence Act, 1998 (Act no 116 of 1998) or Protection from Harassment Act, 2011 (Act No 17 of 2011), and may be disqualified from appointment. The Criminal Law (Forensic Procedures) Amendment Act, Act 37 of 2013 requires that all new appointments in the South African Police Service as from 31 January 2015 provide a buccal (inside cheek) sample to determine their forensic DNA profile. The forensic DNA profile derived from the sample will be loaded to the Elimination Index of the National Forensic DNA Database. Appointments will be made in terms of the Public Service Act, 1994 (Act No 103 of 1994) as applicable to the post environment. Persons who retired from the Public Service by taking a severance package, early retirement or medical retirement, as well as persons with previous convictions, are excluded. The South African Police Service is an equal opportunity, affirmative action employer and it is the intention to promote representivity in the Public Service through the filling of these posts. Persons whose transfer/ appointment will promote representivity will therefore receive preference. The South African Police Service is under no obligation to fill a post after the advertisement thereof. Correspondence will be conducted with successful candidates only. If you have not been contacted within three (3) months after the closing date of this advertisement, please accept that your application was unsuccessful
responsibilities:
Render administrative support functions & administer logistical matters.
Maintain leave records, registers and files.
Answer and screen all incoming calls to the office of the Section.
Type reports, letters, minutes, agendas, handle confidential documents, keeping record of the minutes and monitoring flow of documents to and out of the office.
Maintain good record keeping, filing and bring forward system.
Operate standard equipment (photocopy machine, telephone, computers).
Manage the budget and procurement matters.
Ensure correct vesting of expenditure.
Provide weekly reports.
Manage all office human and physical resources.
Ensure compliance with the Public Financial Management Act (PFMA) and Treasury Regulations, Acts & Policies.
requirements:
Applicants must display competency in the core functions of the post.
Be proficient in at least English and one other official language.
Be a citizen of the Republic of South Africa of which documentary proof must be furnished on the day of the interview.
Grade 12/Senior Certificate/NCV Level 4 or equivalent qualification (NQF level 4 as recognised by SAQA).
Relevant courses in the field of the post will serve as an added advantage.
Knowledge, skills and competencies:
General computer literacy skills (MS Word, MS Excel, MS Office, MS PowerPoint and MS Outlook)
Demonstrate competency in acting Independently, Professionally, Accountable and with Credibility
Good verbal and written communication skills
Sound planning, organizing, administrative and problem-solving skills
Strong interpersonal skills
Customer focus and responsiveness
Be willing to work under pressure and extended hours

Pick n Pay is hiring a Blockman, based in Gauteng.
The Blockman is responsible for cutting, preparing, weighing, packaging and displaying meat products according to customer requirements and company standards. The role involves providing excellent customer service, maintaining product freshness, ensuring food safety and hygiene, and keeping the butchery department clean, organised and fully stocked.
Grade 10 or Grade 12 qualification.
Previous experience in a butchery or meat-handling environment will be an advantage.
Knowledge of different meat cuts and basic meat preparation techniques.
Ability to operate meat-cutting equipment safely, where trained and authorised.
Good customer service and communication skills.
Basic numeracy skills for weighing and pricing products.
Ability to work under pressure in a fast-paced retail environment.
Willingness to work shifts, weekends and public holidays.
Good personal hygiene and attention to detail.
Ability to stand for extended periods and handle physical tasks associated with the role.
Meat Preparation and Processing
Cut, trim, debone and portion meat according to customer specifications and company standards.
Prepare and package beef, lamb, pork, poultry and other meat products as required.
Ensure meat is cut accurately and presented attractively.
Minimise waste through correct cutting, trimming and stock handling.
Operate knives, mincers, bandsaws and other equipment safely, where applicable.
Customer Service
Assist customers with their meat selections and provide information about different cuts.
Recommend suitable cuts for different meals and cooking methods.
Weigh, price and package products accurately.
Respond to customer queries and complaints professionally.
Maintain a friendly, helpful and professional attitude at all times.
Food Safety and Hygiene
Maintain high standards of cleanliness in the butchery, preparation areas and equipment.
Follow food safety procedures and company hygiene policies.
Ensure meat products are stored at the correct temperatures.
Prevent cross-contamination by using appropriate cleaning and handling procedures.
Monitor product quality, freshness and expiry dates.
Wear the required personal protective equipment and protective clothing.
Stock Control and Merchandising
Receive and inspect meat deliveries for quality and quantity.
Rotate stock according to the First-In, First-Out (FIFO) principle.
Monitor stock levels and report shortages or damaged products.
Ensure display cabinets are clean, properly stocked and attractively presented.
Apply correct pricing and labelling to all products.
Report expired, spoiled or unsuitable products to the supervisor or manager.
Health and Safety
Follow workplace health and safety procedures.
Handle sharp tools and machinery responsibly.
Report faulty equipment, hazards, accidents and injuries immediately.
Keep floors dry and work areas free from obstructions.
Follow safe lifting and handling procedures.
Teamwork and Administration
Work closely with the butchery supervisor and other department employees.
Assist with stocktaking and stock-loss prevention.
Follow instructions from management and complete assigned tasks on time.
Report operational challenges and customer concerns to the relevant supervisor.
Comply with company policies, procedures and performance standards.

The role identifies revenue leakage, non-compliance, execution gaps and control weaknesses, and drives corrective action to ensure customer investments are applied as approved and deliver the intended commercial outcomes.
responsibilities:
Commercial Investment Assurance
Conduct risk-based audits of customer discounts, rebates, promotional funding, trade spend and commercial investment programmes.
Validate that customer investments are supported by approved agreements, evidence of execution and accurate claims.
Identify and quantify revenue leakage, over-discounting, duplicate claims, unsupported payments and unauthorised commercial spend.
Assess whether trade investments are implemented as intended and escalate material control exceptions.
In-Trade Execution Audits
Conduct physical audits across outlets, wholesalers, distributors and key accounts to verify agreed execution standards.
Assess compliance with Outlet Health, merchandising, visibility, pricing and promotional requirements.
Confirm that point-of-sale materials, Coolers and other commercial assets are deployed, used and maintained in line with approved agreements.
Validate outlet existence, customer classification and route-to-market execution where relevant.
Pricing and Discount Compliance
Audit customer pricing, discount structures, deal mechanics and promotional offers against approved mandates and governance requirements.
Identify deviations from approved price lists, discount thresholds and commercial approval processes.
Investigate suspected discount abuse, off-invoice leakage, irregular claims or other commercial control breaches.
Provide fact-based findings to support recovery, remediation and consequence management processes.
Risk Identification and Investigation
Use sales, volume, pricing, discount and customer profitability data to identify high-risk customers, channels, territories and transactions.
Conduct targeted reviews in response to anomalies, whistle-blower allegations, management concerns or recurring control failures.
Support Internal Audit, Compliance, Commercial Finance and Legal teams with investigations where required.
